title.narrative: Supporting Fourth Primary Education Development Program

description.narrative: The Fourth Primary Education Development Program will support Bangladesh's primary education system to become an efficient and effective system that provides quality primary education to all Bangladeshi children. The new program will build on the achievements of previous programs with a strong focus on strengthening quality of education, improving access to education, and enhancing institutional management through decentralization. The new program is aligned with the country partnership strategy, 2016-2020 which indicates Asian Development Bank's continued support to primary education.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Quality of primary education improved Indicator: At least 50% of the target for training teachers and teacher educators in the CPD plan achieved (at least 50% of them women) (2017 baseline: 0. 2022 update: 28% of CPD training target achieved) (OP 2.1.1; OP 6.2.1) Progress/Status: Achieved. Target achieved and exceeded, as both the overall CPD training coverage and the share of women trained surpassed the required 50% threshold of the original and revised targets.
In 2024, 383,624 teachers are working in Government Primary Schools (GPSs), including 130,920 men and 252,704 women (65.9% of the workforce). Of the total teachers, 383,700 (female: 251,324 and male: 132,376) and 2,010 officers/educators have received at least one of the trainings (curriculum dissemination training) conducted under the approved CPD implementation plan, covering around 95%.
Source: ASPR 2024, JARM 2024. Data Source: DPE report based on EMIS and/or ASPR
Actual value:

Output: Governance and management or primary education system improved Indicator: 80% of approved contracts (goods and works) in DPE processed through e-GP in the year (2017 baseline: e-GP initiated at DPE. 2022 update: target fully achieved) (OP 6.1.4) Progress/Status: Achieved. In 2025, 100% of approved contracts (goods and works) in DPE processed through e-GP.
Source: DPE report, 8 September 2024. Data Source: DPE procurement progress report Actual value:

Output: Governance and management or primary education system improved Indicator: At least 90% of DPE's division, district, and upazila level drawing and disbursing officers adopted iBAS++ (2017 baseline: iBAS++ introduced in DPE. 2022 update: target fully achieved) (OP 6.1.4) Progress/Status: Achieved. iBAS++ has been rolled out in 100% of all DDOs for the submission of pay bill. Of all DDOs, 90% have been currently preparing budget through iBAS++.
Source: RoD of 6th JCM held on 23 November 2021. Data Source: MOPME report on PEDP4 progress Actual value:

Output: Access and participation to primary education enhanced Indicator: Additional 43,500 gender-segregated WASH blocks, 11,250 safe drinking water sources, and 30,000 classrooms completed according to the Infrastructure Planning Guideline of MOPME and as per standard of the Bangladesh National Building Code (2017 baseline: 24,338 WASH blocks; 39,348 water sources; and 39,003 classrooms completed during the PEDP3. 2022 update: 13,212 WASH blocks; 9,068 water sources; and 9,134 classrooms completed during PEDP4) (OP 1.3.1; 2.1.4) Progress/Status: Achieved. The target was fully achieved and exceeded across all infrastructure components, with all completed WASH blocks meeting gender-segregated and disability-friendly design standards and all infrastructure complying with IPG and BNBC requirements to ensure inclusivity, safety, and full compliance.
In 2025, • 34,620 additional classrooms were constructed, • 44,634 gender-segregated WASH blocks were built, and • 21,598 safe drinking water sources were installed.
All completed WASH blocks meet gender-segregated and disability-friendly design standards, ensuring full inclusivity. All completed infrastructure-including additional classrooms, WASH blocks, and drinking water sources-fully complies with IPG and BNBC standards.
Source: ASPR 2024, ROD of 13 JCM 2025. Data Source: EMIS and/or ASPR Actual value:

Output: Access and participation to primary education enhanced Indicator: Additional 3,000 government schools converted from double-shift to single-shift operations (2017 baseline: 22.6% of existing government schools have single-shift operations. 2020 update: additional 745, or 2% of government schools converted to single-shift) (OP 6.2.1) Progress/Status: Achieved. Target achieved and exceeded, as 4,407 schools were converted from double-shift to single-shift operations during the PEDP4 period, surpassing the target of 3,000 schools.
In 2024, uut of 65,567 government primary schools, only 13,519 (20.6%) operated on a single-shift basis in 2024. The number of single-shift schools increased from 9,112 in 2017 to 13,519 in 2024, reflecting an additional 4,407 schools converted from double-shift to single-shift operations during the PEDP4 period. Data Source: EMIS and/or ASPR Actual value:

Output: Access and participation to primary education enhanced Indicator: Additional 650,000 out-of-school children enrolled in learning centers (50% boys) (2017 baseline: 100,072 [50% boys]. 2022 update: additional 583,893 enrolled [52% boys]) (OP 1.1.1) Progress/Status: Achieved. Target achieved and exceeded, as 964,766 out-of-school children (51.6% boys) were enrolled in learning centers, surpassing the target of 650,000 children.
In 2024, Additional 964,766 out-of-school children (51.6% boys) were enrolled in 33,334 learning centers (LCs) under PEDP4.
Note: The percentage was calculated based on the JARM report. The APSS did not provide sex-disaggregated data.
Source: JARM 2024. Data Source: Bureau of Non-Formal Education endorsed implementation support agency report Actual value:

Output: Quality of primary education improved Indicator: 67,500 newly recruited and existing teachers without DPEd or CinEd (at least 50% of them women) certified through DPEd program (among them, 25,000 certified through updated DPEd program), and 1,200 teacher educators with capacity to deliver the updated DPEd program (2017 baseline: 32,353 teachers with DPEd. Not applicable as regards to training of teacher educators on DPEd. 2021 update: 46,696 teachers without DPEd or CinEd certified through DPEd) (OP 2.1.1; OP 6.2.1) Progress/Status: Achieved. In 2023, the DPEd certification targets were fully achieved and substantially exceeded, with 79,659 teachers trained (64% women), 77,768 certified through the updated DPEd program, and 1,891 teacher educators certified through BTPT. Furthermore, a total of 1,640 teachers certified through C-in-Ed (Certificate in Education).
Source: ASPR 2024. Data Source: National Academy for Primary Education and/or DPE report, EMIS, ASPR Actual value:

Output: Quality of primary education improved Indicator: At least 50.0% of government primary schools meet the student-teacher ratio standard of 40:1 (2016 baseline: 35.4%. 2020 update: 78.3%) (OP 6.2.1) Progress/Status: Achieved. The target for the STR ratio (40:1) was achieved and significantly exceeded of the original and revised targets.
In 2023, 84.04% of government primary schools met the student-teacher ratio standard of 40:1 or less from the original and baseline target (35.4%).
Source: ASPR 2024. Data Source: ASPR Actual value:

Output: Quality of primary education improved Indicator: Revised pre-primary and grades 1-5 curricula and textbooks, and newly developed teaching-learning materials (with selected supplementary reading materials) approved by the National Curriculum Coordination Committee (2017 baseline: grades 1-5 curricula in 2011 version to be updated, and textbooks in 2013 version to be updated; teaching-learning materials, including supplementary reading materials, not made available to schools. 2022 update: Revised pre-primary and grades 1-5 curricula approved) (OP 6.2.1) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. In 2024, the target was fully achieved. NCTB developed and revised textbooks, TLMs, and SRMs for pre-primary and grades 1-5 in alignment with the revised 2021 and 2022 curricula. The MoPME established the National Curriculum Coordination Committee (NCCC) to oversee textbook evaluation and approval, supported by NCTB subcommittees and writers. NCTB produced storybooks for pre-primary and grades 1-5 and identified 173 additional SRMs. Experimental textbooks for grades 1-3 were developed, revised, and distributed, while revised textbooks for grades 1-5 and pre-primary were approved by NCCC and endorsed by MoPME in 2023-2024. All TLMs and SRMs were finalized and approved in October 2024.
Source: RoD of 12 JCM, 5 February 2025. Data Source: National Curriculum and Textbook report Actual value: Y

Output: Quality of primary education improved Indicator: Additional 100,750 teachers (at least 50% of them women) completed training on using ICT and e- teaching-learning resources through ICT training (2016 baseline: 71,862 teachers trained on ICT [men: 23,097; women: 48,765]. 2020 update: 30,805 teachers trained on ICT) (OP 2.1.1; OP 6.2.1) Progress/Status: Achieved. Considering both ICT training and online curriculum dissemination training, the original and revised targets were achieved and significantly exceeded, with a combined total of 459,732 teachers trained against the target of 100,750.
In 2024, additionally, a total of 383,700 (female: 251,324 and male: 132,376) teachers and 2,010 officers/educators have received online curriculum dissemination training. A total of 76,032 (female: 41,001 and male: 35,031) teachers received ICT in Education training.
Source: JARM 2024. Data Source: DPE report based on EMIS and/or ASPR Actual value:

Output: Governance and management or primary education system improved Indicator: A needs and performance-based UPEP piloted for 50 upazilas as per updated UPEP guidelines (2017 baseline: UPEP not funded. 2022 update: target fully achieved) (OP 6.1.1) Progress/Status: Achieved. In 2021, UPEP guideline updated and approved by MoPME. A needs and performance based UPEP piloted in 50 upazilas during the PEDP4 period.
Source: 2nd JCM, November 2019; 5th JCM, May 2021. Data Source: UPEP implementation report Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Y Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Y Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Governance and management or primary education system improved Indicator: Institutional strengthening plan as per the updated ODCBG implemented. (2017 baseline: ODCBG being updated. 2022 update: all activities of the plan initiated) (OP 6.1.1) Progress/Status: Achieved/Partially Achieved. In 2025, There are 36 core ISP activities comprising 55 individual sub-activities. Out of the 55 sub-activities, 41 have been fully achieved, representing 74.55% of the total ISP implementation. An additional 3 sub-activities (5.45%) have been partially achieved. The remaining 11 sub-activities (20.0%) have not yet been achieved, although all necessary processes at the DPE/MoPME levels have been completed, but they require inter-ministerial procedures to be carried out in order to consider them as completed.
According to the revised target, ‘ISP under the updated ODCBG has been implemented.' The target was substantially achieved.
In 2025, as per the revised Memorandum (10 December 2023), which states that the ‘Institutional Strengthening Plan under the updated ODCBG was implemented across eight divisions and 64 districts,' the original and revised targets were fully achieved. Key ISP activities recommended in the ODCBG were implemented nationwide—for example, translating, publishing, and disseminating updated job descriptions for teachers, SMCs, UEO/URC staff, and DPEO/PTI officials. Additionally, the updated SLIP and UPEP guidebooks were implemented: 65,565 schools benefited from SLIP, and 100% of schools received SLIP funds as per the revised guidelines. The UPEP guideline was updated, approved by MoPME, and piloted in 50 upazilas during PEDP4.
Note: Due to the different interpretations of the changes, the performance rating varies. If ISP implementation across 64 districts is considered, the target was achieved. However, if ISP implementation is assessed more broadly, the result is rated as substantially achieved.
Source: 2nd JCM, November 2019; 5th JCM, May 2021; 8th JCM, March 2023; 13th JCM, 7 August 2025. Data Source: MOPME report on PEDP4 progress Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Y Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Y Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Governance and management or primary education system improved Indicator: Integrated web-based EMIS with sex-disaggregated data (including for social groups) made operational in DPE (2017 baseline: some EMIS subsystems exist but are not integrated and not web-based. 2022 update: integration ongoing and on track) (OP 2.3.2; OP 6.1.1) Progress/Status: Achieved. In 2025, the Data System for Decision-Making has been strengthened through multiple initiatives. IPEMIS, with 24 live modules, now serves about 700,000 users in the primary education sector including non-GPSs. E-monitoring has been implemented in all upazilas, supported by ICT dashboards for improved decision-making. A unified database under PEPEMIS, an upgraded data center, and licensed Oracle software ensure stronger system integration. Additional achievements include GIS mapping of schools, uploading six APSCs.
Source: RoD of 13 JCM 2025. Data Source: Integrated EMIS website, MOPME report Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Y Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Y Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Governance and management or primary education system improved Indicator: Student number-based SLIP fund received by 85% of government schools in the year as per updated SLIP guidelines (2017 baseline: 0 [all government schools received flat SLIP fund within the PEDP3]. 2022 update: target fully achieved) (OP 6.1.1) Progress/Status: Achieved. Target Achieved and Exceeded, as fund disbursement reached 100% of schools, surpassing the target of 85%.
In 2023, SLIP guidelines were updated, and all 65,565 schools benefited from the SLIP program. A total of 100% of schools received SLIP funds in accordance with the updated guidelines. The student number-based SLIP fund was disbursed to all 65,565 government primary schools in FY 2022-23.
Source: 2nd JCM November 2019; 8th JCM, March 2023. Data Source: SLIP implementation progress report Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Y Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Y Target year: 2025 Target value: Y
Quality and equity of primary education improved for all children from pre-primary to grade 5

Proportion of grade 3 students with minimum proficiency in Bangla and mathematics increased by 10 percentage points for both boys and girls from the 2017 baseline (NSA 2017 baseline: Bangla - 47% [boys 45%, girls 48%]; and Math - 34% [boys 35%, girls 33%] (OP 1.1.1) Achievement: N Progress/Status: Partially Achieved. In 2022, as per revised target, between 2017 and 2022, Bangla proficiency increased by 4 percentage points overall, and Mathematics proficiency increased by 5 percentage points overall. Data Source: National Student Assessment Actual value: N

National survival rate to grade 5 increased by 2 percentage points for both boys and girls (2017 baseline: 83.3% [boys: 81.3%, girls: 85.4%]. 2020 update: 84.7% [Boys 83.3% and Girls 85.9%]) (OP 1.1.1) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. In 2024, based on the 2021-2024 average, the national survival rate to Grade 5 rose by about 2 percentage points from the 2017 baseline, boys improved by 3.3 points and girls by 2 points. Data Source: ASPR Actual value: Y

Difference in net enrollment rates in grades 1-5 between the weighted average of five lowest performing districts and the national level decreased to 7% (boys: 10%; girls: 4%) (2016 baseline: 9% [boys:12.5%; girls: 5.0%]. 2020 update: 4.7%). (OP 1.1.1) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. In 2023, the reduction in net enrollment rate differences between the five lowest-performing districts and the national average surpassed the 2025 targets across all groups, with the overall gap reduced to 2.2% (boys: 2.4%; girls: 1.9%). Data Source: ASPR Actual value: Y
